# AeroStrat: Intelligence Driven Aviation

> AeroStrat (Intelligence Driven Aviation) is building the next generation of aviation technology: one connected ecosystem for airline operations, spanning training, safety and compliance, flight operations, maintenance and engineering, and network planning, on a single shared foundation set up to each airline's own manuals and authority. Its team pairs 25+ years of experience in the aviation sector with deep technology expertise. AeroStrat started with pilot training, where two products are live with airlines today: AeroStrat EBT/CBTA for evidence-based competency assessment and grading, and AeroStrat TMS for training planning, validity tracking and records. Based in Tallinn, Estonia.

Canonical page: https://aero-strat.com/

## Vision and ecosystem

- **Vision:** To establish the definitive digital operating system for global airlines, unifying fragmented data into a single source of operational intelligence and continuous oversight.
- **Mission:** To engineer intuitive, enterprise-grade technology that eliminates operational silos, transforming complex data into connected intelligence so airlines can optimize performance, elevate safety and drive continuous improvement across their entire ecosystem.

AeroStrat is building one connected technology ecosystem for airline operations on a single shared foundation: one crew list, one record and one login across every module. Training is live; the next domains follow on the same foundation.

1. **Training (live):** AeroStrat EBT/CBTA for competency assessment and AeroStrat TMS for training management, on one pilot record.
2. **Safety & Compliance (next):** occurrence reporting and audit findings tied back to the competency evidence behind them.
3. **Flight Operations (next):** crew qualification, currency and rostering constraints in the same record as training.
4. **Maintenance & Engineering (next):** technical training and authorisation tracking on the shared competency framework.
5. **Network Planning (next):** capacity and crew readiness modelled against the training pipeline.

## Who we are

AeroStrat pairs 25+ years of experience in the aviation sector (flight operations, crew training, regulation and oversight, seen from inside the airline) with deep expertise in software engineering, data and analytics, delivered as secure systems an airline can rely on every day. What it builds follows how airlines are run and regulated.

- **One shared foundation:** every product is set up to the airline's own manuals and authority, and works from the same records.

## Direction

An airline runs on connected disciplines. AeroStrat is building technology for each of them, one domain at a time, on one shared foundation. It started with training.

## The training solution

Two connected products for airline pilot training: one measures how well pilots perform, the other keeps every pilot current. Airlines can take one, or both on a single pilot record.

### AeroStrat EBT/CBTA: every grade consistent, every skill measured

Evidence-based training and assessment, graded by the ICAO, IATA and EASA method on forms built from the airline's own manual.

- Nine ICAO/IATA competencies and all 73 observable behaviours
- Day 2 training planned from the pilot's Day 1 evidence
- Trends by pilot, cohort, fleet and instructor

Details: https://aero-strat.com/ebt-cbta

### AeroStrat TMS: every pilot current, every renewal planned

The training management system: validity, planning, recurrent training, records and audit in one place.

- Every licence, medical, check and course tracked live
- Renewals planned months ahead, pilots reminded before anything lapses
- One digital file per pilot, ready for the inspector

Details: https://aero-strat.com/tms

### One pilot record: entered once, never re-typed

For airlines that take both, the products share one crew list, one pilot record and one login.

- A graded check updates the record and sets the next expiry
- Compliance and competence side by side for the Director
- One audit trail across both products

Built on ICAO, IATA and EASA guidance, set up to each airline's manuals and authority.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is AeroStrat?**
AeroStrat is a next-generation aviation technology company based in Tallinn, Estonia. It is building one connected software ecosystem for airline operations: training, safety and compliance, flight operations, maintenance and engineering, and network planning. Its training products, AeroStrat EBT/CBTA and AeroStrat TMS, are live with airlines today.

**Which AeroStrat products are live today?**
Two training products. AeroStrat EBT/CBTA grades every pilot check against the ICAO nine-competency framework on the airline's own forms. AeroStrat TMS keeps every pilot current with validity control, renewal planning, recurrent training, records and audit. Airlines can take one, or both on a single pilot record.

**What comes after training?**
Safety & Compliance, Flight Operations, Maintenance & Engineering and Network Planning, each built on the same foundation as training: one crew list, one record and one login across every module.

**Which regulators does AeroStrat support?**
AeroStrat is built on ICAO, IATA and EASA guidance and is not tied to one regulator. Each airline is set up to its own manuals and national authority, including EASA and ECAA frameworks.

**Who uses AeroStrat today?**
AeroStrat has been tested for more than 8 months in co-development with two regional airlines: 120+ pilots and 250+ cabin crew, with more than 14,000 grades recorded to date.

**How can we see it?**
Book a live walkthrough on a sample of your own crew, records and check forms at aero-strat.com/contact, or email info@aero-strat.com.

# About AeroStrat

> AeroStrat is a next-generation aviation technology company based in Tallinn, Estonia, building one connected ecosystem for airline operations: training, safety and compliance, flight operations, maintenance and engineering, and network planning. Its team pairs 25+ years of experience in the aviation sector with deep technology expertise. It started with training, where AeroStrat EBT/CBTA and AeroStrat TMS are live today.

Canonical page: https://aero-strat.com/about

- **Vision:** To establish the definitive digital operating system for global airlines, unifying fragmented data into a single source of operational intelligence and continuous oversight.
- **Mission:** To engineer intuitive, enterprise-grade technology that eliminates operational silos, transforming complex data into connected intelligence so airlines can optimize performance, elevate safety and drive continuous improvement across their entire ecosystem.

## Who we are

- **Experience:** 25+ years of experience in the aviation sector. Flight operations, crew training, regulation and oversight, seen from inside the airline.
- **Expertise:** Deep technology. Software engineering, data and analytics, delivered as secure systems an airline can rely on every day.
- **Base:** Tallinn, Estonia. Founded in 2026, a team of six working with airlines and their authorities.

## Products

- **AeroStrat EBT/CBTA** (live): competency assessment and training records. It captures, grades and analyses evaluation data against the ICAO/IATA competency framework.
- **AeroStrat TMS** (live): validity, planning, recurrent training, records and audit in one system, sharing one crew list and one pilot record with AeroStrat EBT/CBTA.
- **What they are not:** neither product delivers e-learning courses. They record, plan and analyse training and assessment.

## Direction: one domain at a time, on one shared foundation

An airline runs on connected disciplines. AeroStrat is building technology for each of them. Training is live; the next domains follow on the same foundation.

1. **Training (live):** AeroStrat EBT/CBTA for competency assessment and AeroStrat TMS for training management, on one pilot record.
2. **Safety & Compliance (next):** occurrence reporting and audit findings tied back to the competency evidence behind them.
3. **Flight Operations (next):** crew qualification, currency and rostering constraints in the same record as training.
4. **Maintenance & Engineering (next):** technical training and authorisation tracking on the shared competency framework.
5. **Network Planning (next):** capacity and crew readiness modelled against the training pipeline.

## Core strategic pillars

- **Connected Intelligence:** elevating passive records into active, cross-departmental forecasting and risk assessment.
- **Architectural Scalability:** a unified technological infrastructure designed to adapt and expand alongside evolving global aviation needs.
- **Operational Clarity:** complex industry data delivered through intuitive, high-visibility interfaces that minimize administrative friction.

## Brand values

1. **Absolute Precision:** data treated with the rigor required on the flight deck.
2. **Architectural Foresight:** every module and workflow engineered to integrate into a wider ecosystem.
3. **Actionable Clarity:** complex metrics distilled into insights that accelerate decisions.
4. **Continuous Integration:** the feedback loop between operational execution, data evaluation and systemic improvement.

## How we work with you: set up from your manuals

AeroStrat staff onboard each airline from its own manuals. AeroStrat builds the airline's check forms from its paper forms, sets its grading scale and document control, and configures the platform to its authority. Building forms is part of the implementation service, not a self-serve builder. Forms stay as they are, whether they start on paper or in digital form. Support and maintenance are included.

# AeroStrat solutions: EBT/CBTA and TMS for airline pilot training

> Two connected products for airline pilot training. AeroStrat EBT/CBTA grades competency by the ICAO, IATA and EASA method. AeroStrat TMS keeps every pilot current and every renewal planned. Both are configured to each airline's own training manual and authority, not tied to one regulator, and every airline's data is isolated from every other's.

Canonical page: https://aero-strat.com/solutions

## 1. AeroStrat EBT/CBTA (competence): every grade consistent, every skill measured

Evidence-based training and assessment for airline recurrent pilot training. Grading, training planning, analytics and records in one system, built on the ICAO, IATA and EASA method.

- 9 ICAO/IATA pilot competencies · 73 observable behaviours in IATA wording · 329 IATA scenarios for Day 2 planning · as many forms as the airline uses, built natively rule for rule
- Modules: competency grading (IATA lowest-of-three rule), forms built from the airline's manual, Day 2 planning, three-altitude analytics and fleet risk board, instructor standardisation, signed PDF and append-only audit log, EBT stage support (conventional checking native; Mixed EBT native for pilot assessment)

Full detail: https://aero-strat.com/ebt-cbta

## 2. AeroStrat TMS (compliance): every pilot current, every renewal planned

The training management system. Validity, planning, recurrent training, records and audit in one place, configured to the airline's Operations Manual and authority.

- 5 status levels checked daily; the worst item sets the pilot's file · 3-year recurrent cycle run per pilot · KPI targets set per airline
- Modules: validity control, expiry engine (OM-D rules, renewal windows, end-of-month counting), 3-year plan and monthly load, recurrent cycle, digital pilot file, reports (MEETS / WATCH / BELOW), pilot portal & email notices

Full detail: https://aero-strat.com/tms

## 3. How they work together: one crew list, one pilot record, one login

For airlines that take both, every step of a pilot's proficiency check writes to the same record, so nothing is typed twice:

1. **TMS plans the check:** the expiry engine sees the operator proficiency check falls due inside the planning window; the pilot is placed in a simulator group and emailed the assignment, with a reminder before the session. An audit entry is written.
2. **EBT/CBTA grades the check:** grades by the airline's rules, a signed PDF generated on submission, live fleet analytics updated.
3. **TMS updates the record:** the completed, graded session updates the TMS record with no re-typing. The expiry engine recalculates the check from its rule (e.g. 6 calendar months, end of month) and the plan drops the pilot from that month. The pilot portal shows the new expiry; the office is notified.
4. **The Director sees both:** validity and competence for the same pilot, fleet and period, side by side. Board-ready reports and an audit pack are one click away.

### What is shared, and who writes it

- **Crew list:** imported from the crew system and matched to every training record; imports are reconciled so gaps are found before the auditor finds them.
- **Pilot record:** the single record both products update (licences, medicals, checks, courses, grades and documents, per pilot).
- **Training rules:** configured per airline by admins; used by the TMS expiry engine and the EBT/CBTA grading engine.
- **Competency grades:** with the observable behaviours, TEM outcome and instructor narrative behind each one.
- **Expiries:** calculated by the expiry engine from the latest record and its rule, never typed; every expiry traced to its rule.
- **Documents:** scans and certificates filed to the pilot, flagged when missing or outdated, plus a signed PDF for every evaluation.
- **Audit trail:** every change, who, when and how it was entered; every save backed up automatically.

Every airline's data is isolated from every other's. Pilot and cabin-crew records are kept separate at the database level, and the data stays the airline's, exportable in full at any time.

## One platform, every role

One login. Each user sees and changes only what their role allows, in both products. Every action is logged.

- **Training Director & admins:** see everything and set the rules: rules, settings and users; KPI reports by fleet and period; the full audit trail; fleet dashboards and the risk board; instructor consistency; policies, standards and alerts.
- **Training office / coordinators:** run the daily work: record training for one pilot or a class; update crew, plan groups, book sessions; import and export.
- **Instructors:** grade on forms built from the airline's manual; plan Day 2 from the pilot's Day 1.
- **Pilots & cabin crew:** self-service, no calls to the office: portal for licence, medical, renewals and upcoming training; email before each expiry; rate each session through a short link, no login; results framed as coaching, not discipline.

## Implementation: four stages, about five weeks

Target timeline from receiving the airline's manual, records and forms. The airline names one owner; AeroStrat does the setup.

1. **Stage 1:** the airline provides its Operations Manual and training manual, current records and forms, and one named owner. AeroStrat reviews them and maps every record to a pilot. Output: scope and plan agreed.
2. **Stage 2:** the airline answers mapping questions. AeroStrat moves records from Excel, paper or the old system, builds forms from the manual and recalculates every expiry. Output: records migrated, forms built.
3. **Stage 3:** the airline reviews rules and standards. AeroStrat loads the crew list, creates accounts, sets up training rules and standards, and reconciles against the source data. Output: Director sign-off.
4. **Stage 4:** the team attends training on live data. AeroStrat trains users on their own data and switches on notices and dashboards. Output: expiries, grades and dashboards live.

The airline owns the programme and keeps every regulatory obligation; the instructor sets every final grade and AeroStrat never overwrites it. Authorities approve programmes, not software.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can we start with one product?**
Yes. Take AeroStrat TMS, AeroStrat EBT/CBTA, or both. Each runs on its own. Together they share one crew list, one login and one pilot record, so a graded check updates the next expiry with no re-typing.

**We already use another platform.**
AeroStrat moves you across. Your forms are digitised, and your past grades and training records are moved into the new system. The migration is done by AeroStrat.

**Do we have to change our forms?**
No. If you have a training manual but no digital forms, AeroStrat builds the forms from your manual, rule for rule. If you already have forms you want to keep, AeroStrat implements those exactly: same structure, same scoring logic, same sign-off chain, so instructors see what they already know, digitised.

**Will our pilots accept it?**
Results are framed as coaching, not discipline. The instructor sets every grade and AeroStrat never overwrites it. Pilots also see their own status in the portal instead of asking the office.

**What happens to our data?**
It stays yours: isolated from every other airline and exportable in full at any time. Pilot and cabin-crew records are held separately at the database level rather than hidden in the interface, so a security review or an auditor gets a verifiable answer about isolation.

**Does it replace our LMS or rostering?**
No. AeroStrat works alongside both. Rostering stays where it is, and AeroStrat does not deliver e-learning. Connecting the TMS to an existing LMS is on the roadmap: where the LMS supports module export, its learning modules can be embedded in the TMS.

**Is the software approved by the authority?**
Authorities approve programmes, not software. AeroStrat supports your compliance with EASA and your national rules, and the airline keeps every regulatory obligation.

**How long does implementation take?**
Four stages, about five weeks, from receiving your manual, records and forms. You name one owner; AeroStrat does the setup.

## Three steps, one decision

Agree a pilot project: one fleet, the products you need, and success measures set in advance. Then share your manuals, records and forms, and go live. Contact: https://aero-strat.com/contact · info@aero-strat.com

# AeroStrat EBT/CBTA: EBT/CBTA assessment platform for airlines

> From paper records to performance intelligence. AeroStrat EBT/CBTA grades every check against the ICAO nine-competency framework on the airline's own forms, and turns every submission into pilot, cohort and fleet analytics. Built on the ICAO, IATA and EASA method (also ECAA). Live, tested for more than 8 months in co-development with two regional airlines.

Canonical page: https://aero-strat.com/ebt-cbta
For: Training Directors, Heads of Training and TRE/TRI leads.

Key numbers: 9 ICAO core competencies · 73 observable behaviours (IATA wording and numbering) · 329 IATA scenarios for Day 2 planning · 3 analytical altitudes (micro, macro, trend) · 4 one-click outcomes on submission.

## The problem: today's tools record the grade, analysis is still done by hand

EBT/CBTA expects grades derived from observed behaviour, trends tracked across the whole pilot population, and proof that every instructor grades to one standard.

- **Paper and spreadsheets (records, not insight):** grades are cut off from the competency framework; every cohort review and audit response is assembled by hand, and a lost file is a gap in a pilot's record. Result: trends surface too late.
- **An existing ETR system (built to file grades):** designed to store training records, with competencies added later. Instructors still work out competency grades by hand, so consistency depends on the individual. Result: instructor variance unseen.
- **Tools built for the methodology (thin where it matters):** analysis usually stops at the individual pilot; cohort trends, fleet risk and instructor standardisation stay manual, and fixed templates make airlines adapt to the tool. Result: insight stays manual.

## Positioning: the EBT/CBTA layer

AeroStrat EBT/CBTA sits alongside the airline's LMS and can be integrated with AeroStrat TMS.

- **LMS (adjacent system):** delivers e-learning content (course hosting, SCORM playback, knowledge checks). AeroStrat does not deliver e-learning.
- **AeroStrat EBT/CBTA:** calculates competency grades against the ICAO nine-competency framework using the airline's own scoring rules. A signed PDF per evaluation, a permanent per-pilot history with a full edit audit trail, and pilot, cohort and fleet analytics.
- **AeroStrat TMS (integrates):** validity, planning and scheduling, on one pilot record.
- **Responsibilities:** the airline owns every regulatory obligation (implementation plan, safety risk assessment, authority submissions). AeroStrat supports it: captures evidence, recommends grades, applies the correct standard and raises policy flags. The instructor decides and sets the final grade; any override needs a written reason. AeroStrat never overwrites it.

## Native to the EBT transition

Whether an airline is starting EBT or already running it, AeroStrat supports the programme at its current stage and carries it to the next, on one platform. Each airline sets its own stage, with a start date, and moves up with the same records, pilots and history. Each check is graded under the stage in force on its date.

- **Stage 0, Conventional ("train, then check"):** native, live. Item by item: satisfactory / unsatisfactory or pass / fail per item, against flight tolerances, on the scale the authority's form uses. No competency framework needed; a task and manoeuvre list instead.
- **Stage 1, EBT principles ("check, then train"):** native, live. A Day 1 proficiency check comes first; Day 2 training is planned from its findings, with ranked scenarios from the 329 in IATA's EBT workbook. The nine competencies are graded 1–5 as the airline's manual defines, with optional observable behaviours and TEM outcomes.
- **Stage 2, Mixed EBT ("evidence-led"):** native for pilot assessment, live. Evaluation phase, manoeuvres validation and scenario-based training; the licence is still revalidated by check. Recommended grades from evidence, interim and final standards, alerts, policies and flags.
- **Stage 3, Baseline EBT ("full EBT"):** partly roadmap. Same engine, cycles and modules: live. Equivalency tables and line-check intervals: on the roadmap.
- **Enhanced EBT:** needs flight-data integration (future plan).

## On submission: one click, four things happen automatically

1. **Calculates competency grades:** nine competencies graded on the airline's scale, following its sign-off chain. Each grade is derived from observed behaviours by the IATA lowest-of-three method.
2. **Generates a signed PDF report.**
3. **Adds a permanent record** to the pilot's history, with the observed behaviours behind each grade.
4. **Feeds live fleet analytics:** fleet dashboard and cohort comparison updated.

## Grading engine

- Every check graded against the nine ICAO/IATA pilot competencies (KNO application of knowledge, PRO procedures & compliance, COM communication, FPA flight path automation, FPM flight path manual, LTW leadership & teamwork, PSD problem solving & decision making, SAW situation awareness, WLM workload management), with all 73 observable behaviours in IATA's own wording and numbering.
- Each exercise is mapped to the competencies it mainly tests and those it supports.
- Recommended grade by the IATA lowest-of-three rule: how many OBs, how often, TEM outcome.
- "Insufficient evidence" instead of a number when evidence is thin.
- Any item graded 1 or 2 needs observable-behaviour evidence.
- The instructor decides; a different final grade needs a written reason.

## Forms: built from your manual

Rebuilt from the airline's own forms at onboarding: items, grading scale per section, attempts, TEM-applicable items and competency mapping, printed in the layout of the airline's paper form.

- Simulator check (OPC/LPC), line check, training & evaluation, cabin crew, remedial training
- The airline's scale per section: S/U/N-A, PASS/FAIL or 1–5
- First and second attempts recorded

## Day 2 planning

The next session is built from what the last check found. The recurrent programme is planned as cycles, modules and two-day sessions, each with an assigned instructor.

- Open a pilot's Day 1 and see which OBs were demonstrated
- Choose the competencies to develop
- IATA Appendix G.V scenarios ranked by coverage, tagged primary or secondary
- A record of who chose what and when

## Analytics at three altitudes

- **Micro (the single evaluation):** a close look category by category, behaviour by behaviour. Numeric or categorical, detected automatically.
- **Macro (the cohort):** compare every pilot in a class, rank or aircraft type. Tells an individual issue from a programme one (one pilot struggled, or the entire class did), which is the input EBT expects in the next recurrent cycle.
- **Trend (the pilot over time):** a chronological view of one pilot's history: improving, plateauing or slipping.
- **Fleet risk board:** a short, ranked list of the pilots to review first, each linked to the pilot's record and trend view.

## Instructor standardisation

Each instructor's average grade is updated with every submission and compared with the fleet mean, with a tolerance band, so standards stay consistent. Supports instructor standardisation in Mixed EBT. Trainees rate each session through a short link (QR), no login. Director dashboard for instructor ratings.

## Records and audit

Submitting a form calculates the grades, generates a signed PDF, adds a permanent record and feeds live analytics at once. Every edit after submission is logged in an append-only audit trail. Below-standard alerts email the training managers. Records export for IOSA and the airline's authority.

## AI coaching assistant

For pilots with two or more checks, a plain-language coaching and remediation summary. Gated on history, just-culture framing, Director-only switch.

## Product status

**Live:** own forms (simulator, remedial, line check, cabin crew) · grading engine (lowest-of-three, your scale) · reports & signatures (signed PDF, audit trail) · micro/macro/trend analytics · fleet dashboard (KPIs, risk ranking, TEM themes) · instructor comparison · AI coaching & fleet report (Director-gated) · trainee feedback (QR, no login) · currency & validity (3-year cycle expiry alerts).

**Planned next:** malfunction and approach equivalency tables · baseline line-check intervals · instructor Mixed EBT.

**Future plan:** Enhanced EBT with flight-data integration · type rating, MPL and ab initio · pilot self-service · offline app.

## Onboarding: fitted to the airline

AeroStrat develops forms from the airline's training manual, with competency mapping, OBs and TEM, or digitises existing forms exactly as they are. Support and maintenance included.

1. **Discovery:** the training manual and any existing evaluation forms, digital or paper.
2. **Build:** each form developed from the manual, or existing forms digitised as they are.
3. **Configure:** rosters loaded, instructor and Director accounts created, departments set.
4. **Go-live:** grading, reporting and analytics run from the first submission.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is AeroStrat EBT/CBTA?**
Evidence-based training and assessment software for airlines. It grades every check against the nine ICAO/IATA pilot competencies and all 73 observable behaviours, on forms built from the airline's own manual, and turns every submission into pilot, cohort and fleet analytics. It has been tested for more than 8 months in co-development with two regional airlines.

**How is a competency grade calculated?**
Each grade is derived from observed behaviours by the IATA lowest-of-three method: how many observable behaviours, how often, and the TEM outcome. When the evidence is thin, AeroStrat shows "insufficient evidence" instead of a number.

**Who sets the final grade?**
The instructor. AeroStrat recommends a grade, applies the correct standard and raises policy flags. A different final grade needs a written reason, and AeroStrat never overwrites it.

**Do we need to be running EBT already?**
No. Conventional checking, EBT principles and Mixed EBT (for pilot assessment) are supported natively and live today. Baseline EBT runs on the same engine, with equivalency tables and line-check intervals on the roadmap. Each airline sets its own stage with a start date and moves up with the same records, pilots and history, and each check is graded under the stage in force on its date. Enhanced EBT, which needs flight data, is a future plan.

**How does Day 2 planning work?**
Open a pilot's Day 1 check and see which observable behaviours were demonstrated, then choose the competencies to develop. AeroStrat ranks scenarios from the 329 in IATA's EBT workbook by coverage, and records who chose what and when.

**Is AeroStrat EBT/CBTA an LMS?**
No. It does not deliver e-learning. It sits alongside the airline's LMS, and can be integrated with AeroStrat TMS on one pilot record.

**Which reports does it produce for audits?**
Every submission creates a signed PDF and a permanent record in the pilot's history. Every edit after submission is logged in an append-only audit trail, and records export for IOSA and the airline's authority.

Contact: https://aero-strat.com/contact · info@aero-strat.com

# AeroStrat TMS: pilot training management system

> Every pilot current. Every renewal planned. AeroStrat TMS puts validity, planning, recurrent training, records and audit in one system, configured to the airline's Operations Manual (OM-D) and national authority. It connects to AeroStrat EBT/CBTA for airlines that subscribe to it. Live.

Canonical page: https://aero-strat.com/tms
For: Directors of Training, Heads of Training and Crew Training Managers.

Key numbers: 5 status levels, checked daily · worst item sets the pilot's status · 3-year recurrent cycle, run per pilot · KPI targets set per airline.

## What changes: fragmented becomes one training system

- **Time:** hours lost to admin. The same dates are typed into spreadsheets, forms and emails; staff check records instead of planning.
- **Errors:** one typo, one lapse. A wrong date or a missed renewal stays hidden until the roster is built or an inspector asks for the file.
- **Legacy tools:** built for another era. Older systems often run on one PC, send no reminders and do not connect to rostering or competency data.

The data already exists. What is missing is one modern system that keeps it current automatically.

## A daily action list, not a spreadsheet

Filter by status, then record a renewal. The expiry is recalculated from the rule and the pilot leaves the list. Items tracked include OPC (operator proficiency check), LPC (licence proficiency check), LC (line check), CRM (crew resource management), DG (dangerous goods), SEP (emergency & safety equipment), class 1 medical and passport.

## Validity control: the worst item sets the status

Every licence, medical, check and course is scored against the airline's own rule. A pilot's overall status is their worst item, so one lapsed check flags the whole file. Status follows the airline's rules, for example: GREEN over 60 days · YELLOW 60 days or less · RED under 30 days · EXPIRED · MISSING.

- Daily action list by fleet, status and item
- Data-gap report for mandatory items with no record
- Red and expired items feed the renewal plan and pilot notices automatically

## Modules: one platform, every training workflow

### Expiry engine: calculated, not typed
Validity periods, renewal windows and expiry counting configured to the airline's OM-D and national authority. Every expiry is traced to its rule; the new expiry is suggested from the rule and reviewed before saving.
- Calendar-month and end-of-month counting
- Renewal windows keep the original expiry
- Medical interval set per pilot, by age and operation
- Check spacing validated against OM limits

### Planning: demand known months ahead
Every renewal placed by expiry and lead time, with the reason shown for each month. Overdue items are pulled into the first planning month automatically.
- 3-year renewal plan by month; monthly load shows peaks before they happen
- Simulator groups aligned to each pilot's check expiry; OPC + SIM shown as one booking
- Email on booking, change and cancellation, plus a reminder

### Recurrent cycle: the 3-year cycle, run per pilot
Phases, base-month groups and checklists built from the airline's recurrent programme. A passed check or course writes the completion and new expiry to the pilot's record.
- Seasonal phases, e.g. cold and hot weather operations
- Base-month groups built from each pilot's check expiry
- Each item: date, result, score, attempts, remedial, simulator hours, feedback
- Lapse warnings for checks that expire before the plan
- Cycle KPIs: completion, on-time, first-pass and remedial rates

### Records: one digital file per pilot
Records, documents and the audit trail, ready for the inspector at any time. Crew-system imports are reconciled against training records, so gaps are found before the auditor finds them.
- Record one pilot or a full class in one step
- Documents flagged when missing or out of date
- Pilot file in six folders; automatic backups; encrypted ZIP export for an inspection
- Every change logged: who, when and how

### Reports: training performance, measured
Monthly, quarterly and yearly reports for the Director, by fleet and activity. Every KPI target is set by the airline's training department.
- Training compliance, on-time renewal and first-pass rate
- Overdue items and data gaps
- First-pass and remedial training rates; simulator utilisation against plan; instructor observations
- MEETS / WATCH / BELOW status, export to PDF or Excel

### Pilot portal & notices: pilots see their own status
- Licence, medical, ratings, qualifications and upcoming training
- Email ahead of each expiry, e.g. 45 days, passports 90
- Planned, changed or cancelled training by email
- Daily digest of changes and expiries for admins

## How it works: one loop, no re-keying

A record entered once updates the plan, the pilot and the reports: results entered once → expiry recalculated, certificate filed (EBT/CBTA grade linked for subscribers) → renewal plan and monthly load rebuilt → pilots booked into simulator, classroom and checks with email notice → live validity, KPIs and audit-ready pilot files for the Director.

## Integration with AeroStrat EBT/CBTA

For airlines subscribed to AeroStrat EBT/CBTA, both systems share one crew list, one pilot record and one login. A completed, graded session updates the TMS record and the next expiry, with no double entry. The Director sees validity, competency trends and instructor concordance side by side, per pilot and per fleet. On the roadmap: connecting to the airline's existing LMS (AeroStrat does not build an LMS).

## Implementation & migration: we move your records, you sign off

From Excel, paper or a legacy TMS, AeroStrat does the full migration and implementation. The training department reviews and approves; it does not re-key records.

- **We migrate:** Excel training sheets, paper records, legacy TMS data, crew master & rosters, training history, certificates & scans, licences & medicals, simulator & check records.
- **We configure:** training rules from the Operations Manual; the recurrent programme (courses, phases, simulator cycle).
- **We validate:** reconciliation against the source data; Director sign-off before go-live.

Every record mapped to the pilot, every expiry recalculated, every document filed in the pilot's digital file. Users are trained on the live system with their own data.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is AeroStrat TMS?**
A training management system for airline pilots. It puts validity control, renewal planning, recurrent training, digital pilot files and audit in one system, configured to the airline's Operations Manual (OM-D) and national authority.

**How does validity tracking work?**
Every licence, medical, check and course is scored against the airline's own rule, and a pilot's overall status is their worst item, so one lapsed check flags the whole file. Five status levels are checked daily, for example green, yellow, red, expired and missing.

**How are renewals planned?**
Every renewal is placed by expiry and lead time on a 3-year plan by month, with the reason shown for each month. Overdue items are pulled into the first planning month automatically, and simulator groups are aligned to each pilot's check expiry.

**Do pilots get reminders before something expires?**
Yes. Pilots get an email ahead of each expiry, for example 45 days before, or 90 for passports, and when training is planned, changed or cancelled. They also see their own status in the pilot portal.

**Can you migrate our existing records?**
Yes. From Excel, paper or a legacy TMS, AeroStrat does the full migration: every record mapped to the pilot, every expiry recalculated and reconciled against the source data. The Director signs off before go-live, and the training department does not re-key records.

**Is the pilot file ready for an inspection?**
Yes. Each pilot has one digital file in six folders, every change is logged (who, when and how), missing or out-of-date documents are flagged, and the file exports as an encrypted ZIP for an inspection.

**Does it work with AeroStrat EBT/CBTA?**
Yes, for airlines that subscribe to both. They share one crew list, one pilot record and one login, so a completed, graded session updates the TMS record and the next expiry with no double entry.

## Three steps, one decision

1. **Live demo:** the TMS shown on a sample of your own crew and training data.
2. **Data & scope intake:** records, rules and manuals shared; quote sized to your crew list.
3. **Migrate · go live:** records migrated, rules configured, team trained, live across the fleet.

# EBT and CBTA glossary

> Plain-English definitions of the terms airline training departments use for evidence-based training (EBT) and competency-based training and assessment (CBTA), from the nine pilot competencies to Baseline EBT and training records.

Canonical page: https://aero-strat.com/glossary

## Training approaches

### Evidence-Based Training (EBT)

A way of running recurrent training and assessment for airline pilots, set out by ICAO in its Manual of Evidence-based Training (Doc 9995). Instead of repeating the same list of manoeuvres every check, EBT develops and assesses a pilot's overall capability across the [core competencies](https://aero-strat.com/glossary#competencies), and uses operational and safety data to decide what is trained. [AeroStrat EBT/CBTA](https://aero-strat.com/ebt-cbta) grades every check this way.

### Competency-Based Training and Assessment (CBTA)

Training and assessment built around defined competencies and the standard of performance expected for each, rather than hours completed or items ticked off. ICAO describes the approach in PANS-TRG (Doc 9868). EBT applies CBTA to recurrent pilot training; CBTA also covers cabin crew, instructors and other aviation roles.

### The nine pilot competencies

The competencies ICAO and IATA use to describe pilot performance. Each one is graded on its own, so a training department can see exactly where a pilot, a cohort or a fleet needs work. Application of knowledge (KNO) was added to the original eight.

1. **PRO:** Application of procedures and compliance with regulations
2. **KNO:** Application of knowledge
3. **COM:** Communication
4. **FPA:** Flight path management, automation
5. **FPM:** Flight path management, manual control
6. **LTW:** Leadership and teamwork
7. **PSD:** Problem solving and decision making
8. **SAW:** Situation awareness and management of information
9. **WLM:** Workload management

### Competency

A dimension of human performance that reliably predicts successful performance on the job. A competency shows in behaviours that draw on the relevant knowledge, skills and attitudes, and it is observed and assessed under set conditions.

### Competency framework

The set of competencies, descriptions and observable behaviours an airline uses for training and assessment. ICAO publishes a reference framework; each airline adapts it to its own operation and has it accepted by its authority. AeroStrat EBT/CBTA is set up to the airline's own adapted framework and manual.

### Observable behaviour (OB)

A single, role-related behaviour an instructor can see during a session and record as evidence for a competency grade. Each competency is described by several observable behaviours, for example confirming that information has been understood, under Communication.

### Threat and Error Management (TEM)

A model for describing how crews manage operational risk. Threats are events outside the crew's control that make the flight more complex, such as weather or a technical fault. Errors are crew actions or omissions that lead away from what was intended. An undesired aircraft state is a position, speed or configuration that reduces the safety margin. EBT scenarios are built and debriefed with TEM.

## The EBT programme

### EBT module

One recurrent training and assessment event in the simulator, normally made up of an [evaluation phase](https://aero-strat.com/glossary#eval), [manoeuvres training](https://aero-strat.com/glossary#mt) and [scenario-based training](https://aero-strat.com/glossary#sbt). Modules follow a multi-year programme, usually three years, so that every competency and training topic is covered.

### Evaluation phase (EVAL)

The first phase of an EBT module: a realistic line scenario flown with as little instructor input as possible. It assesses the crew's competencies and shows what the rest of the module should focus on.

### Manoeuvres training (MT)

The phase of an EBT module where specific handling manoeuvres, such as an engine failure on take-off or a go-around, are practised until they are flown to the required standard.

### Scenario-based training (SBT)

The phase of an EBT module that develops competencies through realistic line scenarios, focused on the training needs found in the evaluation phase. Scenarios are built around threats and errors (see [TEM](https://aero-strat.com/glossary#tem)).

### Day 1 and Day 2

In a programme run on EBT principles, the Day 1 proficiency check comes first and the Day 2 training session is planned from what Day 1 found: "check, then train".

### Flight simulation training device (FSTD)

An approved simulator, such as a full flight simulator, used for pilot training and checking. EBT modules are flown in a qualified FSTD.

## Implementation stages

### Conventional training and checking (Stage 0)

Traditional recurrent training: "train, then check". Each item is graded satisfactory or unsatisfactory, or pass or fail, against flight tolerances on the authority's form. Most airlines still start here. [AeroStrat EBT/CBTA](https://aero-strat.com/ebt-cbta) supports it natively.

### EBT principles (Stage 1)

Conventional checking run with EBT methods: "check, then train". A [Day 1](https://aero-strat.com/glossary#day1-day2) check comes first, Day 2 training is planned from its findings, and the nine competencies are graded 1 to 5 as the airline's manual defines.

### Mixed EBT (Stage 2)

EBT running alongside the conventional programme. Modules include an evaluation phase, manoeuvres and scenario-based training, but the licence is still revalidated by a proficiency check.

### Baseline EBT (Stage 3)

Recurrent training and assessment fully dedicated to EBT. Licence revalidation runs through the EBT programme instead of a separate proficiency check.

### Enhanced EBT

Baseline EBT adapted with the airline's own data, such as flight data and safety reports, so training targets the risks of that specific operation.

## Grading, records and training management

### Grading scale

The scale an instructor uses to grade each competency. EBT commonly uses five points, 1 to 5, as defined in the airline's manual. AeroStrat EBT/CBTA uses the airline's own scale and scoring rules; its default bands run from S1 Unsatisfactory to S5 Excellent. The instructor always sets the final grade.

### Instructor concordance

How closely instructors agree when they grade the same performance, also called inter-rater reliability. Training departments monitor it to keep grading fair and consistent. AeroStrat EBT/CBTA shows each instructor's average grade, updated with every submission.

### Remedial training

Extra training given when a competency is not demonstrated to the required standard, before the pilot returns to the normal programme.

### Training management system (TMS)

Software that plans and tracks crew training: who needs which check or course and when, each person's licences, medicals and validity, and the records an authority audits. [AeroStrat TMS](https://aero-strat.com/tms) does this, configured to the airline's OM-D.

### Validity

The period during which a licence, rating, medical, check or course stays valid. Once it expires, the crew member cannot operate until it is renewed. [AeroStrat TMS](https://aero-strat.com/tms) lists renewals by status: green, yellow, red, expired or missing.

### Electronic training record (ETR)

A digital record of a crew member's training and assessments that replaces paper files. It has to meet the authority's rules on retention and integrity, which is why every change is logged.

### Operator and licence proficiency checks (OPC / LPC)

The simulator checks of conventional recurrent training: the operator proficiency check (OPC) and the licence proficiency check (LPC). In Baseline EBT the EBT programme takes their place for licence revalidation.

### Line check

A check flown on a normal revenue flight to confirm that a pilot operates to the airline's standards on the line.

### Operations Manual Part D (OM-D)

The part of an airline's Operations Manual that sets out its training programmes, checks and standards. [AeroStrat TMS](https://aero-strat.com/tms) is configured to it.

See these terms on your own check forms: book a walkthrough at https://aero-strat.com/contact
